newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent rallies on refinery rumour and Mideast.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent rallies on refinery rumour and Mideast.

text.p: IPE Brent closed higher on Thursday after a late rally prompted initially by locals squeezing stops and built upon by rumours, that were later denied, of a problem at a U.S refinery. Concern about middle east tension added spice to the bullish tone.
"There was talk of an explosion and gasoline put on one penny," said one trader.
June Brent last traded at $18.42 a barrel, up 42 cents, having spent much of the day range-trading in the teens.
Reports that UN oil monitors had been arrested in northern Iraq, also helped the market higher, although the UN said it had no knowledge that any of its personnel had been detained.
"Once we had the push past resistance at $18.25 it took off, it met stronger resistance at $18.35 but broke that as well," said one trader.
Other dealers said volume had been muted throughout the day and the contract was looking good for a small run up.
"Its the combination of middle east news and the fact Brent doesn't seem to want to go below $18.00," said one dealer.

Other middle east news giving a more bullish tint to the market was; the UN inspection team to Iraq saying Baghdad was hiding the extent of its secret weapons programmes, Iranian war-games and the Kuwaiti complaint to the UN about the recent Iraqi attack on two naval vessels.
June Brent's resistance was pegged at $18.65-18.70.
The rally was aided by stronger NYMEX gasoline, which rose 1.16 cents to 62.90 a gallon, and firmer WTI, which broke past the psychological $20.00 a barrel barrier to $20.04, up 31 cents.
Earlier IPE May gas oil had closed $1.75 a tonne stronger at $164.75.
